Simulate data from a stochastic frontier model

Source: R/sim_sf.R
sim_sf.Rd

Generates artificial data from the model estimated by bsfa, for use in examples, tests and prior predictive checks.

sim_sf(
  n,
  beta = c(1, 0.5, 0.3),
  sigma_v = 0.2,
  par_u = 4,
  ineff = c("exponential", "halfnormal"),
  type = c("production", "cost"),
  n_time = 1
)

Arguments

n

number of units. With n_time > 1 the returned data frame has n * n_time rows and the inefficiency term is held fixed within a unit, as in the time-invariant panel model.

beta

frontier coefficients. The first element is the intercept, so a vector of length k implies k - 1 regressors named x1, ..., x(k-1).

sigma_v

standard deviation of the symmetric error.

par_u

parameter of the inefficiency distribution: the rate for ineff = "exponential", the scale for ineff = "halfnormal".

ineff

distribution of the inefficiency term.

type

either "production" or "cost".

n_time

number of periods per unit.

Value

A data frame with the dependent variable y, the regressors, and a unit identifier id. The realised inefficiency terms and efficiency scores are attached as the attributes "u" and "efficiency".

Examples

set.seed(1234)
d <- sim_sf(n = 50, beta = c(1, 0.5), sigma_v = 0.2, par_u = 4)
summary(attr(d, "efficiency"))
#>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
#>  0.4835  0.7801  0.8433  0.8287  0.9470  0.9984
